---
title: "Customise"
---

## Override a single token

Every token in `_pequod-palette.scss` is declared with `!default`,
so any earlier declaration with the same name wins. Drop a tiny SCSS
overrides file into your project and prepend it to the theme list:

```scss
// my-overrides.scss
/*-- scss:defaults --*/

// Crank Starbuck's link colour darker for a print-leaning publication.
$starbuck-light: #00658E !default;

// Or shift the log-50 paper towards a colder white.
$log-50: #F5F2EC !default;
```

Wire it in:

```yaml
format:
  pequod-revealjs:
    theme:
      - my-overrides.scss
      - default
```

The `default` line keeps Quarto's `default` theme participating; the
extension's own SCSS is added by Quarto automatically.

## Replace the body / mono fonts

The font stacks are themselves `!default` tokens. Override in
`my-overrides.scss`:

```scss
$font-family-sans-serif: "IBM Plex Sans", system-ui, sans-serif !default;
$font-family-monospace:  "JetBrains Mono", ui-monospace, monospace !default;
```

If you replace the body font, you almost certainly also want to swap
the `mainfont:` / `monofont:` YAML keys so reveal and Typst pick the
same family up:

```yaml
format:
  pequod-revealjs:
    theme:
      - my-overrides.scss
    mainfont: "IBM Plex Sans"
    monofont: "JetBrains Mono"
```

Self-hosted woff2 fonts can be wired with Quarto's standard
`@font-face` recipe in your own `include-in-header` partial.

## Recolour the data-viz palette

Eight categorical chart slots live in `_pequod-palette.scss` as
`$pequod-chart-1..8-light` / `…-dark`. Override individual slots:

```scss
// my-overrides.scss
$pequod-chart-1-light: #2A2A2A !default;   // softer black for the
                                           // primary series
```

The active set is exported as `--pequod-chart-1..8` CSS custom
properties on `:root` so Observable / htmlwidgets / plain JS can
pick them up at runtime. See [Data viz](data-viz.qmd) for usage.

## Add a logo (once, used everywhere)

The bundled `pequod.lua` filter forwards a single `pequod.logo`
metadata key to the format-specific keys that Quarto / Reveal consume.
Set in your project `_quarto.yml`:

```yaml
pequod:
  logo: assets/logo.svg
```

The filter writes to `meta.logo` (reveal), `meta.website.navbar.logo`
(websites) and `meta.book.navbar.logo` (books), but only if the user
has not already set them.

## Add an Open Graph card image

Same filter, same key shape:

```yaml
pequod:
  og-image: assets/og-card.png
```

The filter resolves `og:image` in this order: `pequod.og-image` →
`website.open-graph.image` → per-page `og-image`. Twitter Card
upgrades to `summary_large_image` when an image is set.

## Per-slide opt-outs (reveal)

Quarto markdown's curly attribute syntax carries through:

```markdown
## A photo wall {.no-footer .no-logo}
```

The deck title slide and H1 section dividers already hide the footer
and logo by convention. `.no-footer` / `.no-logo` only need to be
added on body slides where the corner mark would clash with the
content.

## Highlight pill

Spans marked with `.highlight` or `<mark>` get a warm-paper-deep
background in light mode and a deep-paper-light background in dark
mode. Both `$highlight-bg` and `$highlight-color` are `!default`
tokens; override per-mode in your `pequod.scss` / `pequod-dark.scss`
overrides file.
